intent: The HR "New Employee Onboarding" email is pinned at the top of my inbox but I don't need it there anymore. Unpin it, and pin the "Project Phoenix – Status Update" email from Marcus Thompson instead.

Send an email to sarah.mitchell@contoso.com with subject "Re: Q4 Action Items" and body "Hi Sarah, I'll have the sign-off to you by Thursday." Before sending, make the word "Thursday" bold and italic so it stands out.
Create a new folder called "Review", then move all emails from Priya Sharma into it so I can batch-review her requests later.
Find the "Sprint Demo" event on this week's or next week's calendar and decline the invite.

Sarah Mitchell needs a weekly team update. Send a new email to sarah.mitchell@contoso.com with subject 'Weekly Team Update' summarizing three things: (1) the current status of the accessibility audit from Priya — how many issues were found and how many are Critical, (2) the A/B test outcome for experiment CKO-42 from the Analytics Team — the conversion rate lift and revenue impact, and (3) the critical vulnerability from Priya's dependency audit — the package name and CVE. I need all three points in one email.
Find the "Board Meeting" event on this Thursday. Change the title to "Board Meeting - Rescheduled" and move it to 2:00 PM – 3:00 PM.

Both Priya Sharma and Nina Ross sent me reports waiting for my input. Reply to Priya's accessibility audit email telling her to prioritize the 4 Critical issues in the next sprint. Then reply to Nina's user research summary agreeing that webhook setup and SSO documentation should be top priorities. I need both replies sent.

I need to organize all the periodic reports cluttering my inbox. Create a folder called 'Reports' and move every report-type email into it — that includes the SLA report, the platform metrics, the database performance report, the customer escalation trends, the dependency audit, and the A/B test results. After moving them, flag the ones that have action items I personally need to handle. Don't flag the purely informational ones.

The Analytics Team sent over the final A/B test results for experiment CKO-42 (the checkout flow redesign). Read their email and reply summarizing the key outcome — specifically mention the conversion rate lift percentage and the estimated monthly revenue impact. I need a quick reply on record so the team knows I've reviewed it.

Clean up my inbox. Flag the Azure billing invoice and leave it in the inbox so I can review it later. Archive every other external email (newsletters, GitHub, LinkedIn, npm, Slack, etc.). Don't touch any internal team emails.
Check the SLA report from the SRE Team and reply to them listing which services missed their SLA targets this month. Include the actual uptime percentage for each breached service.
Forward Priya's dependency audit email to Marcus Thompson. In the forwarding note, mention the package with the Critical severity vulnerability and its CVE number — he owns that code.

Nina Ross sent a user research summary about enterprise onboarding friction. Read it and forward the email to Priya Sharma — in your forwarding note, highlight the two onboarding tasks that scored Critical severity and include their success rates. Priya owns the platform UX and needs to prioritize fixes.

I have 4 meeting invites I marked as tentative but I've decided I can't make any of them. Go to my calendar and check the past week as well as the upcoming week to find all tentative events, then decline all four. There is also an upcoming Sprint Planning organized by Marcus Chen — email marcus.chen@contoso.com letting him know I have a conflict and won't be able to attend, then decline that one too.

The weekly platform metrics email from DataOps has a table of top error endpoints. Forward that email to Marcus Thompson and tell him which endpoint has the highest 5xx error count and what its error rate is — he deployed a fix and should verify the numbers.

Do a full mailbox cleanup: go to Deleted Items and permanently delete anything left there from earlier months, but keep the Deleted Items emails from this month. Then go to Junk and permanently delete everything there too, it's all spam.
Jordan Lee sent me a customer escalation trends report. Reply to him confirming I'll handle the most urgent enterprise escalation personally — mention the customer name and their ARR in your reply.

Daniel Lee sent a database performance report before going on PTO. Read it and reply confirming I'll handle the orders table partitioning he recommended. Mention the current size of the orders table and the estimated timeline before we hit performance issues — I want it on record that I've acknowledged the action item.

I need a launch-risk packet ready before the VP SLA review. Create a folder called 'Launch Risks' and move the SLA report, weekly platform metrics report, customer escalation trends report, and dependency audit into it. Flag every one of those except the platform metrics report. Then schedule a 'Launch Risk Review' for the hour immediately before the existing 'SLA Breach Review with VP Eng' event, invite Tom Nguyen, Jordan Lee, and Priya Patel, and summarize the key launch-risk facts from those source emails and reports in the notes, including the breached services, the main /charges issue, the top customer impact, and the critical dependency risk.

I need to connect Nina Ross's onboarding research to Sarah Mitchell's churn numbers. Find Nina's research email, save the PDF locally, and pin it so I don't lose it. Tag Sarah's Q4 revenue dashboard email with a purple category. Then write Sarah a note tying the worst onboarding blockers from Nina's study to the enterprise churn and ARR impact Sarah reported — I want her to see the connection.

Don't schedule another prep meeting — just give Marcus a heads-up. Check the calendar for the week with the Board Meeting and see what else is packed into that Thursday. Email marcus.thompson@contoso.com listing every meeting on that Thursday with its start and end time (exclude lunch). Note which ones overlap or are back-to-back, and include the total meeting hours after accounting for overlaps.

Find Rachel Green's hiring pipeline update. Pin it and mark it yellow so it stands out. Then reply-all confirming the Senior Backend role is our top priority, and cite the current applicant funnel numbers and how much of the recruiting budget we've burned through so far.

Turn my customer-success review into an escalation prep block. Create a folder called 'Enterprise Escalations' and move the customer escalation trends report plus the weekly platform metrics report into it. Then update the existing 'Customer Success Review' calendar event so it becomes 'Enterprise Escalation Review' on the same day as the 'Acme Corp Escalation Call', running 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM, and add Marcus Chen. In the notes summarize the top escalation risk, the relevant /charges reliability signal, and the orders-table storage risk and partitioning timeline from the relevant reports. Finally, forward Jordan's escalation report to marcus.thompson@contoso.com and call out the same escalation and /charges risk.

Before anything else, clean up my view — it's zoomed in and density got changed. Zoom in once, reset zoom to 100%, switch density to Compact and then back to Cosy. Then reply to Priya's auth incident recap — we need to flag tenant-by-tenant blast radius as something to review before sprint planning. Pull the impact numbers from her email.

I need two retention-related items to stay visible in my inbox. Mark Daniel Lee's database performance report as unread so it stays on my radar. Pin Maya Patel's retention audit and tag it red. Then reply to Maya saying you'll plan remediation — reference the retention gap, the policy target, and the account backlog numbers from her audit.

Find Priya Sharma's dependency audit, grab the spreadsheet attachment, and mark the email orange. Forward it to Marcus Thompson — he owns the code for the critical vulnerability Priya flagged. In your note, call out the affected package, the CVE, and how long Priya says the fix will take.

Accept the Metrics Deep Dive: Platform Performance invite on my calendar. Then reply to Jordan Lee's escalation report letting him know I'll personally cover the Acme Corp situation at the meeting — include the revenue exposure and the reliability numbers from his report.

I need a quick launch-blocker note for Tom, not a full packet. Find the launch materials and pin Sarah Kim's readiness matrix. Tag Jordan Lee's escalation report blue. Then write Tom Nguyen an email rolling up the remaining blockers from Sarah's matrix and Jordan's escalation report — cover what's still incomplete, what's missing an owner, and the biggest customer risk.

I need a vendor-cost follow-up packet cleaned up before budget sync. Create a folder called 'Vendor Bills' and move the Azure invoice plus Linda Chen's observability renewal summary into it. Flag the Azure invoice, but leave the renewal summary unflagged. Archive every other external inbox email so only the Azure invoice stays active. Then update the existing 'Vendor Call – Azure' event so it becomes 'Azure Cost Review' on the same day from 4:00 PM to 4:30 PM, add Sarah Kim, and in the notes summarize the Azure billing details plus the observability renewal cost change from Linda's summary. Finally, email tom.nguyen@contoso.com asking him to review the Azure and observability spend, including both the invoice and renewal cost context.

Find Rachel's hiring update and tag her email green. Pin Priya's auth incident recap — it's related. Reply-all to Rachel confirming the Senior Backend role is still top priority, but note that hiring decisions are gated on the auth triage. Cite the relevant numbers from both Rachel's pipeline and Priya's incident.

I want the revenue evidence within reach. Download both attachments from Sarah Mitchell's Q4 revenue dashboard and pin the email. Then forward it to Nina Ross — in your note, highlight the checkout conversion win, the Developer Portal revenue, and the enterprise churn impact from the dashboard.

Before drafting the remediation plan, save both attachments from Daniel Lee's database performance report and mark it unread so I don't lose track. Then reply to Maya Patel's retention audit — acknowledge her findings and connect them to the orders table constraint Daniel flagged. I want Maya to see how the retention gap and deletion backlog she found relate to the table size and the timeline pressure from Daniel's report.

Turn the platform metrics deep dive into a cross-functional escalation review. Create a folder called 'Reliability Escalations' and move the weekly platform metrics report, the customer escalation trends report, and Linda Chen's observability renewal summary into it. Flag the escalation trends and renewal summary, but leave the metrics report unflagged. Then update the existing 'Metrics Deep Dive: Platform Performance' event so it becomes 'Reliability Escalation Review' on the same day from 11:30 AM to 12:15 PM, and add Sarah Kim. In the notes summarize the main /charges reliability risk, customer impact, and observability renewal pressure from the source emails. Finally, forward Jordan Lee's escalation report to sarah.kim@contoso.com and call out the same customer and renewal risk.
